questions.prompt: Why do legacy protocols like SMTP AUTH, POP3, and IMAP4 bypass Conditional Access entirely?
options: Conditional Access explicitly allowlists these protocols
Conditional Access is enforced after first-factor authentication completes through the modern auth stack, which legacy protocols never enter
These protocols are encrypted and therefore invisible to Conditional Access
Microsoft has never supported blocking these protocols
questions.explanation: Legacy protocols authenticate with raw username/password outside the modern auth stack entirely — there's nothing for Conditional Access to intercept or evaluate.

questions.prompt: As described in this lesson, what is the current state of SMTP AUTH Basic Authentication for most existing Exchange Online tenants?
options: It was fully removed for all tenants back in 2022
It remains enabled by default for most existing tenants until it's disabled by default at the end of 2026 (though admins can still re-enable it)
It has never been available in Exchange Online at all
It is only available to tenants created before 2020
questions.explanation: SMTP AUTH was the long-standing exception to the 2022 Basic Auth disablement — it remains a live, currently exploitable gap in most existing tenants until the default changes.

questions.prompt: What's the key difference between Security Defaults and custom Conditional Access regarding legacy authentication?
options: They provide identical protection with no meaningful difference
Security Defaults blocks legacy auth automatically for most scenarios; custom Conditional Access requires an explicit policy, and organizations often carve out exceptions
Custom Conditional Access always blocks legacy auth automatically with no configuration needed
Security Defaults cannot be used alongside Exchange Online at all
questions.explanation: Security Defaults is largely automatic; custom Conditional Access needs an explicit block policy, and real-world exceptions for printers/legacy apps are exactly where this gap tends to persist.

questions.prompt: Why does the lesson connect this topic to the hybrid account-compromise runbook?
options: They are entirely unrelated topics grouped together by mistake
A password reset alone doesn't help if the compromised credential can still authenticate via a protocol Conditional Access never evaluates
The hybrid runbook only applies to accounts using legacy authentication
Legacy authentication automatically triggers the hybrid runbook's double password reset
questions.explanation: If legacy auth remains available and bypasses Conditional Access, a reset password can still be used to authenticate through that path — directly relevant to fully closing off a compromised account.
